outcome: Time to reach cervical dilation of 10 cm
cohort: 526 parturients at Victoria Hospital in London, Ontario, Canada
finding: While labor progression was slower with increasing maternal BMI, cesarean section rates were low across all BMI categories and not significantly different, suggesting that factors like specialized care and patient counseling might have contributed to these findings.
mod_finding: While obese parturients had lower rates of cesarean sections overall, they experienced slower labor progression compared to their normal-weight counterparts.
birth_weight: Infant birth weight was higher in obese primiparous women compared to normal-weight primiparous women.
